input.strategy_title: Reduce default workbench idle culling timeout to 8 hours
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

The default workbench idle culling timeout ships at 24 hours, so abandoned
workbenches hold GPUs overnight and through weekends. Fleet telemetry shows the
median idle-before-stop window admins actually configure is 8 hours. New
clusters should get the sensible default without an admin having to find the
setting.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters is 8 hours instead of 24. Existing clusters with an explicitly configured value are not changed on upgrade. |
| HLR-2 | P2 | The release note and cluster-settings documentation state the new default and how to override it. |

## Affected Components

- Notebooks
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- Per-project or per-user culling policies
- Changes to activity detection (kernel probe behavior)

## Open Questions

None — the setting, its ConfigMap, and the Dashboard administration UI already
exist; only the shipped default changes.

# Ship 8-hour default workbench idle culling timeout

## Description

Change the shipped default workbench idle culling timeout from 24 hours to
8 hours so that newly installed clusters stop idle workbenches after 8 hours
without any admin action. Culling defaults are administered through the
Dashboard (OdhDashboardConfig notebookController settings), which is where the
shipped default value is defined. Existing clusters with an explicitly
configured timeout are not changed on upgrade.

## Scope

- Change the default value of the workbench idle culling timeout in the
  Dashboard's OdhDashboardConfig notebookController culling defaults from
  24 hours to 8 hours.
- Ensure the Dashboard's configuration handling preserves an explicitly
  configured timeout value on cluster upgrade (no overwrite with the new
  default).
- Clusters without an explicit value follow the new 8-hour default.
- The existing Dashboard administration UI for the culling setting continues
  to display and allow override of the value; no UI changes are expected
  beyond any value shown for the default.
- No changes to activity detection (kernel probe behavior) or per-project /
  per-user culling policies — out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A freshly installed cluster with no admin configuration applies a workbench
  idle culling timeout of 8 hours (was 24).
- Upgrading a cluster whose idle culling timeout was explicitly configured
  leaves the explicit value unchanged.
- A cluster without an explicitly configured value uses the 8-hour default
  after upgrade.
- An admin can still view and override the timeout through the existing
  Dashboard administration UI, and the override takes precedence over the
  default.
- Idle culling behavior is otherwise unchanged (activity detection semantics
  untouched).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters
  is 8 hours instead of 24; existing clusters with an explicitly configured
  value are not changed on upgrade.

## Notes

- The change is a default-value flip in existing configuration handling; it
  is revertible by restoring the prior default, and explicitly configured
  clusters are never touched.

# Validate idle culler behavior with 8-hour timeout

## Description

Validate that the notebook-controller idle culler (Notebooks component) works
correctly with an 8-hour idle culling timeout, as the platform's shipped
default moves from 24 hours to 8 hours. The culler requires no code change —
the setting, its ConfigMap (notebook-controller-culler-config), and the
administration UI already exist — but the Workbenches team, which owns the
culler, must confirm the 8-hour behavior end to end and fix-and-retry if it
does not hold.

## Scope

- Exercise the idle culler with the culling timeout configured to 8 hours
  using the existing configuration surfaces (admin UI / ConfigMap).
- Verify workbenches idle beyond 8 hours are stopped, and workbenches with
  recent activity are not culled.
- Verify an explicitly configured timeout value is honored by the culler and
  is not reset by configuration reconciliation.
- Verify culling behavior at 8 hours shows no regressions relative to the
  existing 24-hour behavior (e.g., timing accuracy, last-activity tracking
  via Jupyter server API probes).
- Produce a validation evidence summary (results, environment, any defects
  found and fixes applied).
- No changes to activity detection (kernel probe behavior) — out of scope per
  the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the timeout configured to 8 hours, a workbench idle for more than 8
  hours is stopped by the culler.
- A workbench with recent kernel activity is not culled.
- An explicitly configured timeout value is consumed as-is by the culler and
  survives configuration reconciliation.
- Validation evidence (pass/fail per check, environment details, defects
  found) is documented; any culler defect observed at 8 hours is fixed within
  this epic and re-validated.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The default idle culling timeout for newly installed clusters
  is 8 hours instead of 24 (culler-side validation that the 8-hour value is
  enforced correctly).

## Notes

- This validation can run in parallel with the shipped-default change: the
  culler is configurable today, so the 8-hour value is set directly through
  existing configuration surfaces rather than waiting for the new default to
  ship.

# Document new default culling timeout and override procedure

## Description

Update the release notes and cluster-settings documentation to state the new
8-hour default workbench idle culling timeout (previously 24 hours) and how
administrators override it, so customers are not surprised by the changed
default and know how to restore longer windows.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Release note entry**: state that the default workbench idle culling
  timeout changed from 24 hours to 8 hours for newly installed clusters, and
  that explicitly configured values are preserved on upgrade.
- **Cluster-settings documentation topic**: update the idle culling timeout
  description to reflect the 8-hour default, including:
  - what the default does and when it applies (new installs, clusters without
    an explicit value);
  - how to override the default through the Dashboard administration UI /
    culling configuration;
  - upgrade behavior for clusters with an explicitly configured value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The release note states the new default (8 hours), the prior default
  (24 hours), and that explicitly configured values are unchanged on upgrade.
- The cluster-settings documentation states the current default and provides
  a tested procedure for overriding it.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior
  (shipped default change and culler validation results) and found accurate.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P2): The release note and cluster-settings documentation state the
  new default and how to override it.

## Notes

- Blocked by all implementation work in this strategy: the shipped-default
  change and the culler validation must be complete so the documentation
  describes verified behavior.

| RHAISTRAT-9003-E002 | Validate idle culler behavior with 8-hour timeout | Implementation | Workbenches | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9003-E003 | Document new default culling timeout and override procedure | Implementation | RHAI Documentation | P2 |

## Component Classification

- **Dashboard (active)**: Architecture context states culling defaults are
  administered through the Dashboard (OdhDashboardConfig notebookController
  settings). The shipped default value change is a Dashboard code change →
  E001.
- **Notebooks (passive, different validating team)**: The idle culler in
  notebook-controller consumes the configured timeout; no code change is
  needed (the setting, its ConfigMap, and the admin UI already exist per the
  strategy's open-questions note). Because the passive component is owned by
  the Workbenches team (different from the active component's owner), the
  validation is a separate Implementation epic owned by that team → E002.
- **Documentation (active, docs work stream)**: HLR-2 requires a release note
  and cluster-settings documentation update — substantive content authoring
  on a distinct component → E003 (`docs-authoring`).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001: Ship 8h default (Dashboard)"]
    E002["E002: Validate culler at 8h (Notebooks)"]
    E003["E003: Document default + override (Documentation)"]
    E001 --> E003
    E002 --> E003
```

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring always last) | Documentation must describe the shipped default and its observed behavior; blocked by all Implementation epics. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring always last) | Same — culler validation evidence feeds the documentation's accuracy review. |

E001's own acceptance criteria cover fresh-install default and upgrade preservation. |

All HLRs covered; no orphaned requirements.

None present in the strategy — no overrides to log.

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no

- **Upgrade semantics for implicitly-defaulted clusters**: HLR-1 protects
